When a customer exceeds their limit, the API returns **HTTP 429**, and the response includes a **`Retry-After`** header giving the number of seconds to wait [1]. Rejected requests don't count against the monthly event quota [1].

**How customers know when to retry:** The `Retry-After` value tells them how long to wait. Northwind's SDKs honour this header automatically and back off exponentially [1]. Customers calling the HTTP API directly would need to read the header and wait themselves. The source doesn't say what they should do beyond that.

**Key details:**
- Limits apply per workspace, not per API key. Ten keys in one workspace share one budget [1].
- Short bursts up to 2x the limit are allowed for 10 seconds [1].
- Some endpoints aren't available on certain plans. Those return HTTP 403, not 429 [1].
- Limits vary by endpoint and plan. For example, event ingest on `POST /v2/events` is 100 req/s on Starter, 2,000 req/s on Growth, and 10,000 req/s on Enterprise [1].

**Raising limits:** Enterprise ingest limits can be raised up to 3x the default by contract, through the account team and the Data Plane queue [1]. Growth customers who need more are directed to sales about Enterprise. Temporary backfill raises of up to 72 hours can be granted by the Data Plane on-call primary [1]. The legacy `/v1/track` endpoint will not get higher limits, and customers should move to `/v2/events` [1].

This comes from the internal Engineering page, which the public docs copy on each release [1]. I didn't find a customer-facing version to confirm the wording customers see.

**Harriet Vance (Identity & Billing) is the change approver for Ledger, and Arjun Mehta is her delegate. Both are out November 24–27, so on November 25 neither is available.** The fallback is the VP Engineering, Dmitri Sokolov.

- **Normal change to Ledger:** Billing logic changes need sign-off from the owning team's change approver [1][4]. Ledger is billing-related and Harriet and Arjun handle it [2][4].
- **Availability:** Harriet and Arjun are both out November 24–27 [2]. The policy says that if the approver and delegate are both unavailable, the VP Engineering may approve [1]. Exceptions are logged in `#eng-changes` [1].
- **Freezes:** November 25 is not in a freeze. The month-end billing freeze covers the period up to invoices being sent, around November 2 [1][2]. The holiday freeze starts December 18 [1].
- **Security:** If Ledger is marked "Restricted" in the service catalog, the Head of Security (Tomasz Wierzbicki) or the security on-call delegate must also sign off [1]. The catalog I found doesn't say whether Ledger is Restricted, so check it before filing [3].

Also note that approvals are valid for 7 days [1]. If the change is requested on November 25 and ships later, it may need to be re-requested.

The protocol gives a 30-minute window. If you can't reach the ordering clinician within 30 minutes, the result goes to the on-call medical director, and the 60-minute target is for the result reaching the ordering clinician [1]. You don't keep trying the ordering clinician beyond that point.

**How to escalate:**
- Call the Halcyon answering service at 555-0144 and choose option 2. It pages the on-call medical director. If there's no callback within 10 minutes, it pages the backup [3].
- Don't text physicians' personal mobile numbers. Pages through the answering service are logged and timed, which the chart documentation needs [3].
- Document the time and the person notified in the chart for every critical result notification [1].

The on-call medical director is the person who receives critical lab results when the ordering clinician can't be reached [3]. The November rota covers Wednesday, November 18, but the sources I found don't say who is on duty that day, so the answering service will need to route the page.

Three languages had average connect times above their target last quarter (Q3 2026, July 1 to September 30):

- **Vietnamese** (2-minute tier): average 2:26 [1]
- **Arabic** (2-minute tier): average 2:12 [1]
- **Karen** (5-minute tier): average 6:18 [1]
- **Somali** (5-minute tier): average 5:40 [1]

That's four languages, not three. Vietnamese and Arabic are in the 2-minute tier, and Karen and Somali are in the 5-minute tier. The report's targets are that the interpreter connects within 2 minutes for the top 20 languages and American Sign Language, and within 5 minutes for all other languages [1].

Every other language averaged within its target. Haitian Creole averaged 3:54 and "all other languages" averaged 3:31, both under 5 minutes [1].

Yes. Halcyon pairs every new clinical hire with a **preceptor for 90 days**, which is roughly the equivalent of Northwind's onboarding buddy but longer and more structured [1].

- **Duration:** 90 days.
- **Check-ins:** weekly for the first month, then every other week [1].
- **Competency sign-offs:** the preceptor signs off on a competency checklist at 30, 60 and 90 days [1].
- **First week:** Days 4–5 are shadowing at the home clinic with the preceptor [1].

For comparison, Northwind's welcome guide says the new hire's manager and onboarding buddy walk them through the first two weeks, and the buddy suggests people to schedule 1:1s with [2]. The sources don't state how long Northwind's buddy role lasts.

Both clients put in an idempotency check, so the same job can't send the same thing twice.

**Northwind Labs (October duplicate invoices, INC-2340)**
- Invoice creation is now idempotent per workspace and billing period, which prevents the duplicate invoices [2]. The fix shipped October 8 [5].
- A daily reconciliation report compares invoices against charges. It is marked done [5].
- An open item, due November 6, is an alert for when the payment provider's webhook times out during a billing batch [5].
- The root cause was a webhook timeout that triggered a retry, which re-ran the batch, and invoice creation wasn't idempotent [3].

**Halcyon Health (September duplicate medication reminders, IR-0412)**
- Reminders now carry an idempotency key made of patient, medication and scheduled time. A reminder with an existing key is never sent again [1].
- Scheduler cutovers now require a written runbook and clinical safety sign-off [1].
- Reminder messages now tell patients that if they already took the dose, they don't need to take it again [1].
- The root cause was a September 2 change that ran old and new job runners at the same time, and neither checked whether a reminder had already gone out [1].
